rust/src/accounted_io/fault_plan/adr05_s: Two fresh files receive the same format.
Compare normal formatting with a rule aimed at a write that never happens. Then refuse the second write for lack of space.
The first two images must match byte for byte. The refusal must return an error before the first usable checkpoint appears.
The engine opens an existing volume whose bytes the test saved beforehand.
Refuse the second checkpoint read, then try a separate run where that read returns zero bytes.
Startup must fail in both cases. Reading zero bytes is not a successful read of a block filled with zeros. Neither attempt may change the file.
Block 2 already contains a flushed pattern.
Replace it while the backing write reports zero bytes transferred.
The overwrite must fail and stop the volume. Count one error, no additional completed bytes and no pending work. After reopening, block 2 must still contain the original pattern.
The client overwrites a previously flushed block.
Let the backing sync finish but make it report an error to the engine.
The engine cannot assume success: the flush must fail and the volume must stop. On this particular image the new value must survive because the underlying sync actually finished.
The engine has no room to admit another write.
Attempt a write with a backing-write error rule armed, then request a flush.
The engine must report no space before reaching the rule. This refusal must not stop the volume: the next flush must succeed.
Engine maintenance has written the record identifying a new checkpoint but still needs a final sync before releasing space.
Reject that sync for lack of space.
The engine must keep the earlier checkpoint active, stop serving the volume and reject the next flush rather than reuse space whose release was never confirmed.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-mount.rs::for: The mount helper prepares a filesystem formatter without executing it.
Inspect its executable, arguments, inherited device handle and environment.
The command must invoke the specified system formatter on the already opened device, not resolve a caller-selected program or accept another path.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-mount.rs::inh: The helper must give a child program access to an already opened object.
Prepare its file descriptor for inheritance and start a child process to check it.
The child must retain access after the program starts. The inherited descriptor must not replace standard input, output or error.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-mount.rs::hel: The helper receives simulated kernel information for a block device.
Change its owner, permission flag, block size, capacity or selected filesystem.
Accept the matching device for each filesystem. Reject the others rather than format or mount a device with the wrong owner or layout.
The helper accepts a small set of operations on numbered devices in lab directories.
Parse valid requests alongside unexpected paths, names, flags and argument counts.
Only supported operations with an allowed device number and generated directory name may become actions. The parser must not interpret arbitrary arguments as mount options.
rust/src/bin/fs_support/mod.rs::mount_ch: The helper reads sample mount-table entries instead of mounting a disk.
Change the device identity or source, add another mount, or place a mount below the intended directory.
The checks must distinguish the expected mount from an alias, a nested mount or an unrelated device before the helper proceeds.
rust/src/bin/fs_support/mod.rs::filesyst: Two filesystem types use different lab settings.
Check sample mount data and device sizes using the selected filesystem.
The ext4 check must not accept an XFS mount. Each selection must use its own expected filesystem type and capacity.
rust/src/bin/fs_support/mod.rs::parses_m: The kernel mount table represents some characters in paths with escapes.
Parse sample records containing escaped path characters and malformed fields.
Return the decoded paths and device information for valid entries. Reject invalid records rather than silently comparing the wrong path.
rust/src/bin/fs_support/mod.rs::only_gen: The helper needs to recognize directories created by the lab.
Try generated names and lookalikes with invalid components.
Only the restricted generated name format may pass; a similar-looking caller-supplied directory must not be treated as lab-owned.
rust/src/bin/ublk_support/request_counts: The request counter receives sample reads, writes, flushes and other operations.
Totals must distinguish the operation types without counting a cancelled operation as completed work.
Requests can carry the same operation with different flags, including before the device is ready.
Record example requests, errors and cancellations and print their counts.
The report must retain separate flag combinations, including unknown ones, and show the correct counts and sector totals.
The request counter has limited space for distinct flags and finite numeric counters.
Exceed the available entries or the maximum representable count.
The counter must mark its evidence incomplete rather than present truncated or wrapped totals as a complete workload.
The counter has a report ready to write.
Give it an output buffer that cannot hold the report.
The report operation must return the output error. A partially written report must not be reported as a successful export.
rust/src/format_v4/budget.rs::division_i: The engine divides a limited memory budget between buffered writes, mapping lookups, cleanup and other bookkeeping.
Calculate sizes for small and large volumes and try allocations that do not fit.
Honor the minimum budget and proportional growth, account for each component, and reject a configuration that needs more memory than allowed.
rust/src/format_v4/data_record.rs::every: A disk record groups one or more blocks of client data under a footer.
Encode and decode each supported block count at two positions within a disk region.
The decoded record must identify each payload block at its original address and reject a request beyond its last block.
rust/src/format_v4/data_record.rs::data_: A link record directs the log into a new disk region.
Encode a data record immediately after the link and locate its payload blocks.
The payloads must start in the new region, not after the previous record in the old region.
rust/src/format_v4/data_record.rs::rejec: The test builds a valid footer that identifies two data blocks.
Alter addresses, unused fields, placement, length or checksum, including changes with a freshly computed checksum.
The decoder must refuse inconsistent or damaged records rather than associate a payload with the wrong client block.
rust/src/format_v4/descriptor.rs::descri: A checkpoint descriptor tells the engine where to start recovery.
Encode a known descriptor, inspect the byte positions and decode it again.
The identifying fields and checksum must match the specified disk layout; the two checkpoint slots must occupy distinct reserved blocks.
The decoder receives a checkpoint descriptor and an expected slot.
Vary fields, lengths, checksum or slot identity in controlled inputs.
It must reject invalid descriptors without crashing or treating damaged bytes as a usable recovery point.
rust/src/format_v4/descriptor.rs::equal_: The engine compares the two saved descriptions of a volume.
Vary the descriptions at the same log position, and compare checkpoints across volume growth.
Two descriptions claiming the same position must agree. A legitimate change in backing size across checkpoints must not by itself invalidate the pair.
rust/src/format_v4/format_plan.rs::forma: The formatter knows the logical size, backing capacity and expected maximum fill.
Compute candidate region sizes and change the amount of client data that must fit.
Choose the largest qualifying region size, switching to a different size when the previous layout cannot meet the requested fill.
The formatter receives proposed sizes and fill targets before creating any file.
Try misaligned, invalid or insufficient capacities alongside an accepted boundary case.
Reject invalid combinations rather than constructing an unusable layout; the valid boundary must still produce a plan.
A format plan must cover both client data and the tables that describe physical regions.
Ask for fill beyond the logical volume size and for a backing layout beyond the table limit.
Cap useful fill at the client-visible size and refuse geometry the tables cannot represent.
rust/src/format_v4/geometry.rs::geometry: The geometry calculator translates volume and backing sizes into fixed-size regions and mapping pages.
Calculate counts and tree sizes at representative boundaries.
The resulting layout must cover the requested addresses with the expected number of regions, pages and index levels.
The engine holds a current description of disk capacity.
Try invalid sizes, enlarge the backing store, then request a smaller or invalid replacement.
Only representable geometry and valid growth may succeed. Growth must not reduce the existing storage bounds.
rust/src/format_v4/heads.rs::head_cursor: An append cursor must leave space for the link that moves writes to the next region.
Advance toward the end of a region, then start again after a link.
Payload room must exclude the link slot and restart at the correct capacity in the new region.
rust/src/format_v4/heads.rs::append_plan: The append planner estimates space without writing any data.
Vary payload and metadata counts with room for a full record, a partial group or only a link.
Its counts of blocks, records, links and new regions must match hand-counted layouts, including footer space.
rust/src/format_v4/heads.rs::opening_a_n: The engine reserves regions so that maintenance can still run when client space runs low.
Calculate available space when opening a new client write region while the reserve is depleted.
Moving the write cursor must not manufacture client capacity: only the space left after honoring the reserve is available.
rust/src/format_v4/heads.rs::reserve_and: The space calculator separates maintenance capacity from space a client may consume.
Vary available regions and remaining room at the append position.
The reserved region count and the user-visible space must agree with the allocation plan rather than charging the same region twice.
rust/src/format_v4/index_page.rs::index_: An index page holds addresses for locating lower-level mapping information.
Encode and decode known pages at both supported levels and inspect their fields.
Each child address must occupy the expected position, and the page must round-trip only when its layout is valid.
An index page has a known volume, level, position and permitted children.
Submit pages with malformed references or with identity fields that do not match the expected page.
The decoder must reject them instead of letting a valid-looking address take recovery to an unrelated page.
rust/src/format_v4/mapping_index.rs::sna: A mapping index tracks which saved pages are out of date.
Replace snapshot references in the index and inspect the pages marked for rewrite.
Changing a child must mark its direct index page and affected parents, so writing an index cannot leave old pointers above a changed mapping.
rust/src/format_v4/mapping_page.rs::mapp: A mapping snapshot stores block addresses using a layout inherited from an earlier disk format.
Encode known entries with the newer header, inspect their positions and decode the result.
The entries must retain the expected layout while the header and record boundary identify the current format.
rust/src/format_v4/mapping_page.rs::reje: A decoder receives a saved mapping page with a known identity.
Alter fields and try entries using the reserved address bit.
Malformed snapshots and unrepresentable addresses must be rejected, not interpreted as locations containing client data.
rust/src/format_v4/mapping_page.rs::mapp: A saved mapping page has separate integrity checks for its frame and contents.
Damage its body and test the frame and full-page decoders separately.
Recovery may still recognize the record boundary when only the contents are damaged. It must not accept the damaged mappings as valid.
rust/src/format_v4/reclaim/scheduler.rs:: A scheduler tracks elapsed time between background maintenance runs.
Continually report completed requests up to the maximum interval.
Even without an idle gap the scheduler must say maintenance is due at the deadline and record the completed maintenance run.
The scheduler has a short idle wait and a longer maintenance deadline.
Advance a simulated clock across both thresholds and record late maintenance.
Becoming idle must not imply that the deadline expired. Wake-up hints and lateness must use the applicable threshold.
A scheduler must check for maintenance within its maximum allowed interval.
Construct one with a 200 ms idle wait but a 100 ms maximum interval.
Construction must reject the contradictory timing requirements with the expected assertion, not start a scheduler that can sleep past its deadline.
rust/src/format_v4/reservation.rs::reser: The write reservation calculator estimates physical space before accepting logical writes.
Combine pending payloads, mapping snapshots and transitions between regions.
The required space must include data footers, snapshot records and boundary costs. Reject inputs whose total cannot be represented.
The engine must reserve enough room even if cache pressure forces mappings to be saved at different times.
Enumerate small changed-block sets and alternative save schedules.
For every tested ordering, the calculated reservation must cover the payload blocks, their record metadata and the snapshots actually needed.
rust/src/format_v4/segment_table.rs::fla: The segment table represents region state and write position using compact flags.
Encode supported combinations, decode their fields, and try undefined or incompatible bits.
Valid flags must recover the intended state and write position. Invalid bit patterns must not become ordinary region states.
rust/src/format_v4/segment_table.rs::tab: A segment-table page stores state flags and sequence numbers in separate arrays.
Encode a page containing different region states, inspect byte offsets and decode it.
Each flag must stay paired with the correct sequence number, including a region waiting for release.
rust/src/format_v4/segment_table.rs::las: The final segment-table page may describe fewer regions than a full page.
Encode and decode entries around a page boundary and try a value outside the final partial page.
Valid boundary entries must survive unchanged. Unused slots must not advertise regions outside the backing file.
rust/src/format_v4/segment_table.rs::tab: A valid segment-table page is expected at one position in one volume.
Alter state bits, sequence numbers, unused bytes or identifying fields and recompute integrity fields where appropriate.
The decoder must reject inconsistent entries and pages from the wrong location, even when a checksum alone would not expose the change.
rust/src/format_v4/segments.rs::allocati: The allocator tracks free regions and regions still waiting for discard to finish.
Repeatedly request a free region while some low-numbered regions are unavailable.
Choose the lowest eligible free region, never one still awaiting discard. Reject an impossible initial region configuration.
rust/src/format_v4/segments.rs::freeing_: A region is no longer needed in memory, but an older saved checkpoint can still refer to it.
Advance the release through checkpoint publications and simulate recovery from the earlier checkpoint.
Do not free the region on the first publication. After fallback, publish the pending release again before permitting reuse.
rust/src/format_v4/segments.rs::table_pa: The segment table tracks which pages changed and which metadata references remain live.
Change region state, enlarge the table, then load saved entries.
Changed pages and references must be accounted for. A page restored from saved state must not be marked dirty solely because it was loaded.
rust/src/format_v4/segments.rs::conserva: The engine accounts for allocated regions and references into them.
Check a valid allocation and then present inconsistent reference information.
The conservation check must detect a dangling reference rather than accept space as both available and in use.
rust/src/format_v4/small_records.rs::seg: A link at the end of a region must name another valid region.
Encode and decode links, including one pointing to itself and one beyond backing capacity.
Valid links must preserve their destination. Recovery must reject destinations that would loop in place or leave the backing file.
rust/src/format_v4/small_records.rs::bac: A growth record stores both the previous and new backing sizes.
Corrupt the new size outside the header checksum, or propose no growth, shrinkage or an invalid previous size.
A valid growth must round-trip. A readable header alone must not make a damaged or inconsistent change in size acceptable.
rust/src/format_v4/small_records.rs::dis: A discard record identifies a range of logical blocks that no longer need their old data.
Encode ranges at the start and end of the volume, then try empty and invalid ranges.
Valid ranges must decode to the original endpoints; a discard must not authorize removal outside the volume.
rust/src/format_v4.rs::header_has_exact_: The disk record header identifies the record type and its place in the log.
Encode known fields and decode each supported type.
The bytes must occupy the specified positions and each supported kind must round-trip; an unknown write-head identifier must not be accepted.
rust/src/format_v4.rs::rejects_versions_: Recovery needs a valid header before it can interpret a record.
Feed the decoder unsupported versions and types, nonzero reserved bytes, short buffers and damaged header bytes.
Each invalid input must produce an error rather than a guessed record type or address.
rust/src/format_v4.rs::frame_rule_follow: Within a region, the next record must follow the previous boundary. A region link starts a different sequence.
Validate example data records in both positions.
Only the payload span consistent with the preceding boundary or new region start may be accepted.
rust/src/format_v4.rs::frame_rule_reject: A proposed record includes its current and previous boundaries.
Try a backward chain, reserved checkpoint blocks and metadata spanning several blocks, alongside a valid data span.
Reject the invalid placements without rejecting the permitted multi-block data layout.
rust/src/format_v4.rs::metadata_trailer_: Metadata has a record frame and a separate integrity check over the contents.
Alter bytes in each part and try to recognize the boundary separately from reading the complete record.
A frame can remain recognizable when the body is damaged. Damaged contents must not be returned as valid metadata.
rust/src/io_accounting/tests.rs::create_: A ledger file records storage operations under a fixed byte budget.
Try to create one with zero budget and try creating a second ledger at an occupied path.
Both requests must fail; creating a ledger must neither accept an unusable budget nor overwrite existing evidence.
rust/src/io_accounting/tests.rs::only_on: A ledger reader already exists and one writer holds the right to update it.
Open a second writer without closing the first.
The second attempt must return immediately with a would-block error rather than allow concurrent changes to the same counters.
rust/src/io_accounting/tests.rs::readers: An independent reader watches the ledger while the writer records operations.
Take snapshots before and after completions.
The pending count must reflect operations still in flight. Completed operations and byte totals must appear exactly once after the writer records their outcomes.
rust/src/io_accounting/tests.rs::zero_le: The accounting layer receives an operation with a declared byte count.
Ask it to begin a zero-length data transfer.
The accounting writer must reject the invalid request rather than reserve budget or count an operation that transfers no bytes.
rust/src/io_accounting/tests.rs::budget_: A writer has a ten-byte lifetime budget.
Reserve six bytes for a write that fails, then request five more.
The failed write must use its reservation without adding completed bytes. The next request must report no space; the reader must see the error and exhausted budget.
rust/src/io_accounting/tests.rs::exact_b: A ledger writer has a finite remaining write allowance.
Submit a write whose size reaches the budget exactly and record successful completion.
The writer must admit the operation rather than reject equality at the limit. The completed-byte count must include the entire write.
rust/src/io_accounting/tests.rs::dropped: A writer begins a tracked operation but never explicitly reports success or failure.
Drop the object responsible for recording completion, then inspect the ledger and try reopening the writer.
Mark the totals incomplete instead of guessing how many bytes reached storage. Refuse restart from that incomplete accounting state.
rust/src/io_accounting/tests.rs::new_wri: A writer reserves four bytes and exits with the operation still pending.
Open another writer and read a snapshot of the original ledger.
Refuse to resume rather than invent a completion. Keep the pending operation and four reserved bytes visible to the reader.
The ledger sequence number indicates that an update started but never finished.
Attempt to open a new writer against that interrupted state.
The new writer must refuse to modify the ledger. The original odd sequence number must remain available as evidence of the interruption.
rust/src/io_accounting/tests.rs::reserva: Ledger counters have finite ranges for both reservations and completions.
Place counters near their limits and attempt updates that would overflow.
The writer must not wrap counters and silently admit more work. The visible pending count must remain consistent after rejection.
rust/src/io_accounting/tests.rs::subproc: A writer and a separate reader process share the same on-disk accounting ledger.
Run the reader while the writer changes the ledger.
The reader process must observe the expected updates through its own mapping and exit successfully, without relying on in-process variables.
rust/src/logging.rs::level_names_round_t: A log setting can be supplied as text and displayed again.
Parse each supported level name and try invalid names.
A supported name must reproduce its original level and printed form; unsupported text must not select a level.
rust/src/logging.rs::each_level_permits_: Messages and logging configurations have ordered levels of detail.
Compare each configured threshold with candidate message levels, including disabled logging.
The filter must allow precisely the messages at or below the configured level and never treat the disabled level as a message to emit.
rust/src/mapping_cache/clock.rs::rejects: The mapping cache uses a clock-like cursor to choose an entry to replace.
Construct the replacement policy with space for zero entries.
Construction must fail rather than leave a cursor that cannot refer to any valid cache slot.
rust/src/mapping_cache/clock.rs::second_: The cache replacement policy remembers which entries were recently accessed.
Touch selected entries and repeatedly ask for a replacement as the cursor passes the end of its array.
A recent entry must get a second chance, and the cursor must wrap without losing track of the next eligible slot.
rust/src/mapping_cache/clock.rs::dirty_s: A changed mapping must not be evicted until it has been saved.
Exclude dirty entries from replacement and ask the clock policy to scan a partially or entirely protected cache.
It must choose only eligible entries and stop after a bounded scan even when no entry can be evicted.
rust/src/mapping_cache/clock.rs::one_slo: The clock policy stores recent-access flags in machine words.
Exercise a one-slot cache and capacities around a word boundary, allowing only the last slot to be evicted.
The policy must find that slot without losing or misreading a flag at the boundary.
rust/src/mapping_cache/clock.rs::rejects: A one-slot replacement policy has only slot zero.
Tell it that slot one was accessed.
The expected bounds assertion must fire. A caller error must not modify an unrelated bit or produce a plausible replacement decision.
rust/src/mapping_cache/tests.rs::mapping: The test constructs a mapping cache with no entries loaded.
Inspect the size of a mapping entry, initial occupancy and memory accounting.
The empty cache must report its allocated storage accurately, including slots, lookup structures and replacement-policy bookkeeping rather than just payload bytes.
rust/src/mapping_cache/tests.rs::budget_: A mapping cache has a byte budget and a finite number of pages it could ever use.
Calculate its capacity near rounding boundaries, the minimum allocation and the page-count ceiling.
The chosen capacity must fit whole slots and must not reserve more pages than the volume can address.
rust/src/mapping_cache/tests.rs::rejects: The sizing calculation receives the requested logical volume size and cache capacity.
Try invalid geometry, impossible capacities and sizes whose arithmetic would overflow.
The calculator must reject unrepresentable allocations while still accepting the largest supported logical volume.
rust/src/mapping_cache/tests.rs::default: The cache size is derived from an allowed memory budget.
Calculate the default capacity at representative budgets, then price a cache with one more slot.
The selected size must fit. Where memory is the limit, the next larger size must exceed the budget.
rust/src/mapping_cache/tests.rs::synthet: An unmapped region can be represented by a clean mapping page containing only zeros.
Look up the same synthetic page twice in the cache.
Only the first lookup should be a miss. Reuse the cached zero page on the second lookup without treating it as a changed page that needs writing.
rust/src/mapping_cache/tests.rs::dirty_p: A small mapping cache contains changes that have not yet been saved.
Request another page, publish the dirty mappings and retry the lookup.
The cache must not evict unsaved changes. After publication the retry can proceed, and hit, miss and replacement counters must reflect the actual operations.
rust/src/mapping_cache/tests.rs::invalid: The cache holds known mappings, including a page with unsaved changes.
Try to update or load a page using invalid input.
Report the error without changing existing mappings or clearing the dirty flag. A subsequent lookup must still see the earlier contents.
rust/src/mapping_cache/tests.rs::cancell: A lookup misses and reserves the opportunity to load a page.
Cancel the miss before installing the replacement.
No clean page should count as evicted, and the cancelled lookup must not permanently consume a cache slot.
rust/src/mapping_cache/tests.rs::determi: A small cache repeatedly handles a deterministic mixture of mapping lookups and updates.
Compare the changing cache with a separate reference mapping through evictions and pressure to save changes.
Results must agree throughout, while the storage reserved for the cache must not grow with the number of operations.
rust/src/mapping_cache/tests.rs::hashmap: The cache uses a lookup table with preallocated space.
Replace entries repeatedly at capacities near internal allocation boundaries.
The lookup table must reuse its allocated space instead of growing as old entries leave. The number of resident pages must stay within the selected capacity.
rust/src/mapping_cache/tests.rs::dirty_u: The cache is already allocated and contains changed mappings.
Update pages, retry under cache pressure and iterate or snapshot the cache while counting allocations.
These normal operations must not request additional heap memory once the cache is initialized.
rust/src/mapping_cache/tests.rs::sorted_: The cache can list changed pages in order and fetch a page before it is requested.
Exercise ordered iteration and prefetch with a bounded cache while measuring allocations and inspecting counters.
The work must stay bounded and allocation-free, and a prefetched page evicted before use must be counted as unused.
rust/tests/compaction_small.rs::overwrit: A newly formatted file provides a 128 MiB logical disk with 185 MiB of backing space.
Fill every client block with a recognizable pattern, then overwrite blocks and reopen the file.
The engine must reclaim at least one region and, after restart, return the expected version of every block rather than an earlier copy.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::excl: Two processes can reach the same backing file under different names.
Keep an exclusive lock in one process and attempt a competing open before and after the owner exits.
Aliases must not bypass the active lock. Once the owning process releases it, the file must no longer appear permanently busy.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::pars: The device program accepts distinct commands for creating, serving and deleting a device.
Parse supported command lines with their arguments, including a delete request for device seven.
The parser must return the corresponding operation and preserve the supplied values without performing the operation.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::form: A format request needs a logical volume size and backing allocation size.
Parse requests with and without an explicit maximum fill and try malformed sizes.
When no fill target is supplied, plan for the full logical volume. Reject missing or invalid required sizes instead of guessing storage requirements.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::reje: The formatter exposes a restricted set of size options in MiB.
Try repeated options, old byte-based aliases and options that would force a region size.
The parser must refuse these requests rather than silently picking one of two conflicting sizes or bypassing layout planning.
The device command parser expects a known subcommand and a valid device number for deletion.
Offer unknown or incomplete commands, a negative identifier and trailing arguments.
Return a parse error, not an operation against an unintended device.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::form: The formatter receives a new path and valid logical and physical capacities.
Create the backing file, then open the volume with the engine and inspect its geometry.
The file and client-visible disk must have the requested sizes and use the region size selected by the format plan.
The same raw capacity is tested with two expectations for how full the logical disk will become.
Request the default full-fill layout, then explicitly allow partial fill.
The first request must fail without creating a file; the permitted partial-fill layout must format and reopen with the planned region size.
A file at the requested format path already contains recognizable data.
Ask the formatter to create a new volume at that path.
It must report that the file exists and preserve the original bytes instead of truncating or replacing the file.
The formatter receives invalid or insufficient capacity for a proposed layout.
Test the error path against a missing file and an existing file with sentinel contents.
The invalid request must not create a new backing file or modify the existing one before reporting the layout error.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::inva: An operator may request optional accounting when creating the backing volume.
Provide invalid ledger configuration and separately omit accounting entirely.
A bad ledger must stop setup before the backing file appears. With no ledger requested, the optional step must return no writer rather than an error.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::read: The device program announces its readiness by writing a device path.
Capture the readiness line in a test writer, then make the writer fail during flush.
The complete line must be written and flushed explicitly. A flush error must reach the caller rather than producing a false readiness indication.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::conf: The device adapter builds the parameters it would advertise to Linux for a 37-block disk.
Inspect the configuration without starting a kernel device.
It must advertise the matching sector count, block sizes, cache behavior and discard limits, without advertising unsupported zoned-device operations.
The device adapter derives a queue size from its request and memory limits.
Build controller settings for a sample device and compare them with the expected settings.
Use a single queue with the calculated depth. The test checks the configuration, not I/O through a running kernel device.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::cach: The engine receives a cache budget through the device-serving configuration.
Issue writes across mapping pages using the request flag that requires data to be durable on completion. Reopen the volume and read it.
The engine must use the selected cache configuration and return the written data without requiring a later client flush.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::serv: The service limits request size, simultaneous memory use and the time between maintenance checks.
Validate default settings and vary timing, memory fractions, block alignment and request limits.
Invalid combinations must fail; valid limits must produce a queue depth that fits the configured memory.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::conf: The adapter selects control flags before creating a Linux block device.
Inspect those flags without creating a live device.
The configuration must enable an unprivileged device and leave user recovery disabled. Enabling the former must not accidentally request the latter.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::stop: A separate control thread handles the request to stop a device.
Send the recorded device identifier to a test stop operation and capture the executing thread.
The operation must receive the intended identifier and run on the stop thread, not on the caller that requested shutdown.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::meta: The kernel can attach a metadata hint to a read or write.
Decode otherwise identical requests with and without the hint, including invalid address or length combinations.
The hint must not change the logical operation or weaken normal validation of its geometry.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::fail: Some read flags ask the device to fail promptly instead of retrying.
Decode reads with these hints and compare their results with ordinary reads, including malformed and unsupported requests.
Supported hints must preserve the normal read and its bounds checks; unsupported flag combinations must still be refused.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::acce: A write may ask for durable completion using the force-unit-access flag.
Decode writes, reads and flushes carrying that flag and requests with unknown bits.
Only supported writes may use the durability flag. Other operations and unknown flags must return an unsupported-operation error.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::deco: The adapter translates kernel request descriptors into engine operations.
Supply valid operations and descriptors with invalid alignment, bounds or unsupported operation numbers.
Only exact supported requests may reach the engine. Invalid geometry and unsupported operations must report their respective errors.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::disc: The request adapter operates on a formatted backing file with known client data.
Issue discard and write-zeroes requests, then reopen the volume and read the affected and neighboring blocks.
The cleared range must read as zeros after restart, without clearing unaffected neighbors.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::adap: A four-block volume receives requests through the device adapter, without a live kernel device.
Write a pattern at sector 16, flush with stale address information in the descriptor and reopen.
The flush must succeed without interpreting the stale address as a data range. Only the intended logical block should contain the pattern.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::mult: The device adapter receives one request spanning more than a single logical block.
Write a multi-block pattern, reopen and read the covered blocks and a neighbor.
The engine must place each part in consecutive logical blocks and leave the neighboring block unchanged.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::fata: A queue receives an operation that makes its engine unusable.
Complete that request, then present additional work and combine the queue and close outcomes.
Return the original failure to the waiting caller, reject later work without invoking the failed engine, and report the shutdown error.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::latc: An accounting limit leaves no backing-write budget after the engine opens its test volume.
Issue the first foreground write through the queue.
The client must receive the original no-space error, the volume must enter the failed state, and the queue must record that it cannot serve further work.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::maps: The adapter must translate storage errors into Linux request completion codes.
Pass representative capacity, integrity and fatal engine errors through its error mapping.
Preserve the no-space result for capacity failures and report an input/output error for unusable or corrupt storage rather than inventing a successful byte count.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::reje: A device write descriptor requests a full block, but the supplied data buffer is too short.
Submit the malformed request and then read the intended block with a correctly sized buffer.
Reject the short request before engine I/O. The subsequent read must return the unchanged original data.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::fetc: The queue may already have fetched a request when shutdown or failure begins.
Exercise accepted and rejected paths with counters for engine calls and completions.
Complete each fetched request exactly once. A rejected request must not invoke the engine or report that client bytes were transferred.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::sign: The daemon installs a temporary signal handler for stopping work.
Exercise the signal path in a child process and inspect the handler after cleanup.
A shutdown signal must prevent new work, and the previous handler must be restored rather than affecting later users of the process.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::shut: One queue request has begun when shutdown is requested.
Try to advance shutdown while work remains in flight, then finish that work.
Do not stop the queue underneath the active request. Once the queue enters the stopping state it must reject new engine work.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::daem: Daemon shutdown collects results from several distinct operations.
Return an error from each stage in turn, combine multiple errors and test a clean shutdown.
The combined result must preserve the relevant failures rather than report success because the last stage succeeded. All-success inputs must still return success.
rust/src/bin/block-storage-ublk.rs::shut: Queue completion and closing the engine can fail independently.
Combine a successful queue with a close error, a queue error alone and both failures together.
The caller must see the applicable errors, including both causes when neither queue shutdown nor engine close succeeded.
